newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate firms, baht eases near close.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate firms, baht eases near close.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate rose to 12.50 percent on late Friday and will open at 14.00 on Monday against 11.00-11.75 on Friday morning, dealers said.

They said rumours against the baht in Singapore in late morning triggered a new round of active dollar buying which would erode baht liquidity early next week when related baht/ dollar contracts are due.
The baht weakened further to 25.337-25.342 to the dollar near the Friday close from 25.334-25.337 in the morning and 25.322-25.332 late on Thursday.

A Thai Farmers Bank dealer said rumours of troubles faced by finance and brokerage firms sharply raised demand for local baht funds and pushed up the overnight inter-finance rate to about 15.00 percent from 11.50-12.00 in the morning.
"We're exhausted. The phone rang all day from finance companies seeking to borrow. We could not lend them as we need reserves to square our positions," the dealer said.

Dealers said Thai banks would need to set aside a combined 3.55 billion baht on Monday to buy their quotas of Bangkok Bank of Commerce's shares and invest an additional equal amount later in its convertible debentures.

Rumours on finance firm problems from Thursday afternoon have been denied by the central bank and the stock exchange, and related finance firms have clarified their financial positions to counter market jitters.
The baht/dollar mid-rate was fixed at 25.32 against 25.31 on Thursday.
